chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir Al-Momineen () said: 'Do not initiate the greetings with the women nor invite them to the meal, for the Prophet () said: 'The women are inarticulate and exposed, therefore veil their inability to express themselves with the silence, and veil their exposure with the houses'.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for men when greeting and inviting women according to the Prophet and Imams?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes a specific etiquette for male-female interaction, advising men not to initiate greetings or invite women to meals, based on the Prophet’s description of women as 'ayy (lacking eloquence) and 'awrah (needing covering). Shia scholars interpret 'ayy as a reference to their natural inclination or rhetorical style, while 'awrah signifies the need for modesty and seclusion, prescribing silence and domestic boundaries to honor and protect them.
